Class TiLink

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.ti.TiLink
public final class TiLink extends Object
A TI-84 Plus family calculator on the USB Host Shield, reached with its ordinary computer cable: the board plays the part of TI Connect and sends variables to the calculator over TI's USB link protocol ("DUSB"), so a program can put sensor readings into the lists L1 to L6 for a STAT PLOT. 
TiLink calculator = new TiLink();               // once, at startup
int[] temperatures = new int[TiLink.MAX_LIST_LENGTH];
if (calculator.connect()) {
    calculator.sendList(2, temperatures, count, 0);   // L2 = temperatures[0..count), no decimals
}

DusbTransport carries the packets; this class speaks the commands: mode set, request to send (name, size and the type, archived and version attributes), variable contents and end of transmission. The calculator answers a request with a data acknowledgement, or delay acknowledgements first while it is busy. It takes variables at the home screen and in most menus; an app such as EasyData may keep it busy until it is closed.

Allocation: the constructor allocates the transport's buffers; connect() and sendList(int, int[], int, int) are allocation-free. Calls never throw: they return false and lastError() says which step failed.

  • Method Details

    • connect

      public boolean connect()
      Starts the shield, enumerates the calculator, checks it is a TI-84 Plus family model, selects its configuration, agrees on the raw packet size and puts it in normal mode. Returns false with lastError() set when any step fails.

    • isConnected

      public boolean isConnected()
      Whether connect() succeeded and no transfer has failed since.

    • sendList

      public boolean sendList(int list, int[] values, int count, int decimals)
      Sends count values as the real list L<list> (1 to 6), replacing it: value i is values[i] / 10^decimals, so decimals 1 sends 235 as 23.5. Returns false with lastError() set when the calculator does not take it.

    • sendList

      public boolean sendList(int list, long[] values, int count, int decimals)
      sendList(int, int[], int, int) for values past an int, up to the calculator's fourteen digits: a YYYYMMDDHHMMSS time stamp such as 20261121163005L arrives exactly.
